name: Japanese gohan rice
assumptions: Yield estimated from 300g uncooked rice at ~75g per serving (standard for Japanese gohan as a side dish, yielding ~4 portions after cooking and absorption); mirin, pickle juice, and spring onions are flavorings/garnishes not affecting serving count.
Total time is sum of explicit steps: ~5-7 min rinsing/soaking + 15 min simmer + 15 min rest + ~5 min final stir/serve, conservatively rounded to 45 min total prep/cook.

Mirin classified as potentially containing alcohol (not strictly vegan in all definitions, but treated as compatible here per common recipe usage); sushi rice, spring onions, and pickle juice assumed fully plant-based.

Gluten-free is null due to unspecified mirin and pickle juice (some brands use barley or wheat-derived ingredients); soy is null due to possible dashi option in instructions (could contain soy sauce).
No explicit animal products, dairy, eggs, tree nuts, peanuts, sesame, or shellfish in listed ingredients or instructions.
Assumes 'pickle juice' is from vegetable pickles (e.g., not fish-based) and spring onions are standard green onions.
instructions:
STEP 1
Rinsing and soaking your rice is key to achieving the perfect texture. Measure the rice into a bowl, cover with cold water, then use your fingers to massage the grains of rice – the water will become cloudy. Drain and rinse again with fresh water. Repeat five more times until the water stays clear.

STEP 2
Tip the rinsed rice into a saucepan with 400ml water, or 200ml dashi and 200ml water, bring to the boil, then turn down the heat to a low simmer, cover with a tight-fitting lid with a steam hole and cook for 15 mins. Remove from the heat and leave to sit for another 15 mins, then stir through the mirin. Remove the lid and give it a good stir. Serve with any or all of the optional toppings.

ingredients.name: Sushi Rice
ingredients.assumptions: Standard uncooked sushi rice (short-grain Japanese rice); values for raw/dry state before rinsing and cooking as per typical package data.

ingredients.name: Mirin
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tbs mirin ≈ 15 g (typical tablespoon weight for sweet rice wine); values typical for mirin.

ingredients.name: Pickle Juice
ingredients.assumptions: Garnish pickle juice assumed as ~10 g (small drizzle/splash for flavoring a rice dish); values approximated from typical Japanese pickle brine such as takuan or similar light vegetable brine.

ingredients.name: Spring Onions
ingredients.assumptions: Garnish spring onions assumed as ~20 g chopped (a small handful sprinkled on top); values for raw edible portion.
